head: d3dc4c2c6
scope: receipt PII exposure on printed ticket
summary: Walk-in resolver does NOT auto-create per-customer Users — it resolves to one canonical sentinel User per system, keyed by a stable email. There is no anti-fraud surface for random phone/email injection on the walk-in path itself (the resolver ignores any input). The receipt printed ticket carries operator_name + siret + vat_intra + legal_footer + register_id — no customer phone/email is rendered on the ticket markup. The fiscal increment endpoint is atomic, branch-scoped, idempotent, and audit-chained with best-effort tolerance. Three real findings: (1) walk-in lookup endpoint exposes the resolver-created sentinel user email which is fine since it's a known sentinel, but the existing PosController endpoint does NOT require an open cash drawer (acceptable per design); (2) print-receipt POST has no per-minute throttle (see Architect ARCH-PS4-006); (3) the kiosk localStorage persistence test asserts no PII leakage — good sentinel.

findings.title: Walk-in is NOT a per-customer auto-create surface — no spam/fraud vector
findings.evidence: WalkInCustomerResolver::resolve() always operates on the SAME row (email=walkingcustomer@example.com — a single class constant). It cannot be tricked into creating a second user; firstOrCreate is keyed on that stable email. PosController::walkInCustomer (L149-162) takes no input beyond the auth context, and the implicit auto-resolve in normalizePosRuntimePayload (L224-228) overrides only when customer_id<=0. There is no path where caller-supplied phone/email/name reaches the resolver. RED-team's hypothesised vector (random phone/email allowed?) is rebutted by the code.
findings.recommendation: Document this invariant in the resolver class-level docblock (`@invariant the walk-in resolver creates AT MOST one User row in the entire database`). Add a Feature test that hits the endpoint 5 times and asserts User::where('email', WalkInCustomerResolver::EMAIL)->count() === 1.

findings.title: Walk-in user email IS exposed by /api/admin/pos/walk-in-customer — known sentinel, not a leak
findings.evidence: L156-160 return {id, name, email} — email is the sentinel `walkingcustomer@example.com`. The test asserts that field at L33. The endpoint is gated by `auth:sanctum` + permission:pos (the abort_unless at L151) + throttle:pos-quote (120/min). Since the email is a class constant and not a real customer PII, exposure is not a privacy concern. It is, however, a soft signal of the resolver pattern visible to any operator with pos perm — acceptable.
findings.recommendation: Optional: trim the response to {id, name} only — the email is not consumed by the JS caller (Vuex action only uses customer_id). Not a P-rated issue.

findings.title: Walk-in resolver does NOT require an open cash drawer session — by design for the lookup, but verify the actual order-create path enforces it
findings.evidence: L151 checks only `$request->user()?->can('pos')` — no cash drawer guard. The constructor middleware that enforces cash drawer (`ensureCashDrawerSessionOpen` at L120-143) covers `store` but NOT `walkInCustomer` or `quote` (verified by re-reading the controller; the constructor wiring only attaches to certain actions). The walk-in lookup is a pre-order data-helper, so this is acceptable — the cash drawer guard fires when the operator actually commits the order via POST /admin/pos/. The receipt print endpoint (PosReceiptPrintController::increment) also does not check cash drawer state, which is appropriate (re-printing a delivered ticket should not depend on the current drawer session).

findings.title: Receipt printed-ticket markup does NOT expose customer phone/email
findings.evidence: Full review of ReceiptComponent.vue lines 1-322 (paper-print zone). The rendered fields are: company_name + branch.address + branch.phone (the RESTAURANT phone, not the customer), order_serial_no, order_date, order_time, order_items (qty/name/variations/extras/tax/price), subtotal/tax/discount/delivery/total, order_type, payment lines, queue_number/token, fiscal_sequence_no, audit_fingerprint, legal_footer, operator_name, siret, vat_intra, register_id. No `order.user.email`, no `order.user.phone`, no `order.address` rendering. The kitchen receipt block (L268-318) similarly omits customer PII.
findings.recommendation: Good. Lock with an E2E captures spec: render a delivery order with a known customer phone, capture the printed-ticket DOM, assert phone string is absent. Already implicitly covered by kioskReceiptPersistence spec L54-70 which guards the same invariant on the kiosk side.

findings.title: OrderUserResource DOES expose user.phone + user.email in the OrderDetailsResource — that's the API surface, not the printed ticket
findings.evidence: OrderUserResource L24-25 exposes phone+email; OrderDetailsResource L57 wraps the order's user in this resource. A POS Operator hitting GET /admin/orders/{id} will see the customer's PII. This is by design (refund/contact flow) and gated by permission:order-show middleware on the route. The walk-in user's PII surfacing is benign (constant sentinel). For real customers, this is intentional disclosure to authorised staff.
findings.recommendation: Cross-check with PS-A authz audit — confirm permission:order-show is required for all paths reaching OrderDetailsResource. Out of PS-4 scope, flagged for cross-zone review.

findings.title: Fiscal increment endpoint — atomic + branch-scoped + audit-chained — strong default posture
findings.evidence: L43-48: single atomic UPDATE with branch_id filter prevents cross-tenant increment. L50-52: 404 if no row updated (cross-tenant attempt → 404 not 403, no oracle). L67-93: audit chain emission with best-effort fallback (try/catch + report()). The action string distinguishes first vs reprint (L83): `pos.receipt.reprint` for the legal duplicata trail. payload includes both `print_count_before` and `print_count_after` so the auditor can reconstruct the sequence even without ordering by created_at.
findings.recommendation: Solid. Add a Feature test asserting that calling increment with a foreign branch_id returns 404 (cross-tenant containment). May already exist — verify in tests/Feature/Pos/.

findings.title: kioskReceiptPersistence helper has an anti-PII sentinel test — locks the no-leak invariant on localStorage
findings.evidence: Test 2 (L54-70) attempts injection of customer_email/customer_phone/iban into the persisted snapshot and asserts none of those values appear in the serialised localStorage. The kiosk auto-print recovery (F5 / page refresh) therefore cannot leak operator-side PII to the next kiosk session.
